title: Muse Is Unleashing a World of Pettiness on Instagram
gist: Users are discovering that Meta's AI assistant Muse can identify Instagram accounts that don't follow them back and mass-unfollow them without triggering spam flags, sparking a viral 'reciprocity' cleanse across X, Instagram and Facebook. The trend shows agentic AI taking real actions inside Meta's own platforms, even as Meta pulled an ad touting a weekly 'who unfollowed you' feature.

themes.theme: Muse as an in-platform action agent

insights.claim: Meta's AI assistant Muse can, from a single natural-language prompt, list Instagram accounts that don't follow a user back, export them to an Excel sheet with usernames, real names, classifications and profile links, and unfollow them on request; one user's run identified 151 such accounts within minutes.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Meta's first-party assistant can take agentic actions on its own social graph, a capability third-party apps were banned for, giving Meta a native agent advantage.

insights.claim: Users favor Muse for mass unfollowing because, unlike third-party follower-purge apps that have gotten accounts kicked off Instagram, using Meta's own assistant does not get accounts flagged as spam.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Platform owners can monopolize automation on their own services, disadvantaging third-party tool developers.
insights.locator: Khalil Roberts had heard horror stories

insights.claim: The Muse unfollow trend spread virally across X, Instagram and Facebook in November, with some users saying they downloaded Muse solely for this feature and one claiming to have unfollowed more than 1,000 accounts.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Narrow, socially charged use cases can drive AI assistant downloads more than general-purpose features.
insights.quote: I downloaded Muse just to do this only,

insights.claim: In October Meta removed an ad campaign promoting Muse's ability to 'see who unfollowed you each week,' according to Business Insider, and did not explain the decision to WIRED.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Meta appears wary of surfacing a feature that could reduce engagement or follow-graph density on Instagram.
insights.locator: In October, despite the seeming popularity of the feature

insights.claim: Colorado State University researcher Natalie Pennington says people outsourcing small social decisions to AI partly reflects avoidance of emotionally uncomfortable tasks, and that platform-level data now available at a click is not necessarily information people need.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: AI assistants exposing hidden social-graph data could shrink follow networks and change engagement dynamics on social platforms.
insights.quote: But it doesn’t mean it is something you need to know.

insights.claim: Beyond grudges, some users such as sweepstakes hobbyists use Muse to clean up years of cluttered follows, prompting it to surface a few profile links at a time for manual unfollowing.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Feed-curation by AI could reduce follower counts for giveaway and promotional accounts that rely on accumulated follows.
insights.quote: Your following list can finally work for you instead of the other way around,
